text:
ashley: kicking off apac-southeast2 GPU cluster bring-up. TF apply completed but new nodes are stuck NotReady. tagging in case this blocks handoff.

kevin: can you paste `kubectl get nodes` and `kubectl get pods -A | grep gpu`?

ashley: sure, from one of the bootstrap masters: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes
NAME                         STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
apac-s2-m-1                  NotReady   <none>   4m    v1.25.3
apac-s2-m-2                  NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.25.3
apac-s2-worker-gpu-1         NotReady   <none>   2m    v1.25.3
\n$ kubectl get pods -n kube-system
NAME                                              READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
nvidia-driver-daemonset-abcde                      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          2m
node-problem-detector-xyz                          1/1     Running            0          3m
kubelet-health-check                               0/1     Pending            0          2m
```

kevin: CrashLoopBackOff on the driver DS. `kubectl describe pod` shows `failed to register with kernel: i/o error`? any node-level logs?

ashley: grabbed kubelet logs on apac-s2-worker-gpu-1: 
```
Jan 12 03:14:10 kubelet[1234]: E01012 03:14:10.123456   1234 kubelet.go:230] "Failed to start Kubelet" err="system clock skew detected: certificate validation failed"
Jan 12 03:14:10 kubelet[1234]: I01012 03:14:10.123457   1234 server.go:345] Syncing to API server failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
```

lina: time skew during image provisioning — we saw this before when VM images didn't run cloud-init NTP properly. Looks like the bootstrap AMI's NTP service didn't start, certificates appear outside validity window.

deploy-bot: TF apply finished: module.gpu_pool: 4 resources added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed (:package:).

sam: ok, plan: 1) don't roll forward traffic to this pool. 2) try a quick fix: reboot node with cloud-init triggered, or run `sudo systemctl start chronyd` via ssh to one node and see if certificates revalidate. 3) if that fails, fallback to create temporary on-demand pool (smaller) so Dedicated tests can continue.

kevin: ssh to node shows cloud-init exited early with error `Unable to reach metadata server`. Our bootstrap script waits for metadata but doesn't retry long enough under APAC network flakiness. Need a small upstream TF patch to increase wait timeout and ensure chronyd is enabled.

ashley: I'm going to manually start chronyd on one worker, will update.

(roughly 2m later)

ashley: started chronyd, time synced, kubelet moved to Ready for apac-s2-worker-gpu-1. However nvidia-driver DS still CrashLoopBackOff with `unknown firmware version` in logs.

kevin: driver crash log: `failed to load nv-kernel-module: incompatible module version 2.43 vs driver 3.1` — looks like AMI baked with an older driver than driver-daemonset expects. We have mismatch between baked AMI driver and containerized driver version.

lina: that's the race: earlier AMI build step ran a driver install, then golden image pipeline updated container driver tagging — mismatch. Quick fix: patch DS to use the older driver image tag matching AMI, or rerun AMI build to align. Patching DS is faster.

sam: agree patch DS to match AMI for now. I'm creating a canary: `kubectl set image daemonset/nvidia-driver-daemonset nvidia-driver=registry/redwood/driver:ami-compat-2.43 --record` then monitor GPU nodes.

oncall-bot: Reminder — if GPU pool remains unstable for >30m escalate to oncall rota. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-bringup

(5m later)

sam: patch applied, driver pods rolled, nvidia-driver pods are now 1/1 Running on worker-gpu-*. kubelet and device-plugin healthy.

ashley: summary: root causes = (1) cloud-init/metadata timeout on APAC images causing NTP skew and kubelet cert errors, (2) AMI/container driver version mismatch from uncoordinated image pipeline. Remediations: increase metadata wait/retry in bootstrap, ensure chronyd enabled by default, add gating to image pipeline to validate driver tag parity.

kevin: operational note on capacity/cost — we briefly considered spinning on-demand nodes. decision: keep spot-backed pool but add a small on-demand fallback pool in TF for the first 24 hours in new regions to avoid handoff sloshing. we'll track cost delta under Optimize dashboard.

lina: adding follow-up tasks to the handoff doc and tagging product infra board. I'll open a PR for the TF wait and a CI check for driver tag alignment.

ashley: handoff to infra-sre for post-mortem and long-term runbook updates. Monitoring alerts quieted. :white_check_mark:
